kaynak: The Illustration of History in Persian Manuscripts Figure 3 "A later copy of the Jami‘ al-tawarikh, produced in Turusht [which was near the town of Rayy (near present-day Tehran)] in 935/1529 and now in St Petersburg from the library of the shrine at Ardabil, contains 29 paintings, including the exploit of Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah crossing the Indus (Figure 3).57 This is a double-page painting (the only one in this manuscript), showing the sultan on the left-hand page, not looking at all like someone who has just plunged across the Indus, but standing with his beautifully caparisoned horse and wiping his sword dry with a blue cloth. It reflects the text to the extent that he still has his shield over his shoulder and has planted his banner defiantly on the bank. Perhaps more interesting is the right-hand side of the painting, which shows Chinggis Khan turning back towards his sons and entourage, remarking on Jalal al-Din’s valour." The Illustration of History in Persian Manuscripts page 10
